blocks.text: Mendel did not know about chromosomes. Once his work was rediscovered, biologists linked his 'factors' to chromosomes, and this explained both his laws and the cases where his laws fail.

items: Gene linkage: genes on the same chromosome tend to be inherited together, which counters independent assortment.
Crossing over: exchange of segments between homologous chromosomes in meiosis I, which separates linked genes and modifies the progeny.

blocks.prompt: Which process can separate two linked genes?
blocks.explanation: Crossing over between homologous chromosomes during meiosis I.

items: Linkage keeps genes on one chromosome together; crossing over recombines them.
